reader.requirement: At --std 85 the compiler must accept RESERVE integer-1 [AREA | AREAS] in the file control entry, integer-1 being an unsigned nonzero integer LITERAL (§1985:III.2: no data item, no sign, no zero, and no constant-name exists in 1985), and refuse a missing integer, a zero, signed, decimal, nonnumeric or figurative operand, a data-name, and the 1974 NO/ALTERNATE forms; the witness covers the accepted forms only.

reader.edition-search: grep RESERVE in VersionConformancePass*.cs and FileControlBinder*.cs; followed integerOperand into ConstantEntryBinder and IntegerOperandPass; fileReserveClause grammar has no predicate.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 a constant-name cannot stand for integer-1 (refused); from 2002 an integer constant-name can. The literal forms behave the same.

reader.notes: The grammar spells the format with a superset integerOperand, and the integer-operand machinery narrows it at 85 to an unsigned nonzero integer literal, with an edition arm that refuses a word because 1985 has no constant-name. Every accepted and refused form probed matches the 1985 format and the §1985:III.2 integer definition.
